maria (sec): Heads up — found a CVE impacting tokenizers wheels we vendor for dedicated deployments: CVE-2026-4242. It looks like a metadata parsing bug in manylinux wheels that can cause path traversal when extracting ELF segments. linker-level, not pure Python.
jon (ml): link?
maria (sec): https://nvd.example.org/CVE-2026-4242 (internal mirror). Affected packages: tokenizers < 0.14.2, some transformers builds pull older wheels via poetry lock.
priya (platform): Oof. On Redwood Private we pin wheel artifacts; Dedicated not impacted if using our validated images, but hosted could see CI failures when building custom stacks.
devon (infra): CI already started failing on nightly when we regen lockfiles — saw `auditwheel` errors during wheel repair. Failing job: `python-build-manylinux` on macstadium runners.
sam (sre): Any immediate exploitability? data plane only? KMS keys at risk?
maria (sec): Not KMS compromise. It's local extraction vulnerability — could be used by a malicious wheel to overwrite files during install. That risks startup scripts reading secrets if install runs as root (our containers do run `pip install` as root in some images).
jon (ml): That explains the new failing test in model-ci where transformer's `pip install -r requirements.txt` was overwriting `/etc/ld.so.conf.d` during a build — we blamed packaging script earlier.
priya (platform): Action plan suggestion: 1) temporary block vulnerable wheel versions in pip constraints; 2) regen poetry.lock to bump tokenizers to >=0.14.2; 3) add `--use-feature=truststore`? (not sure) 4) add CI check to fail if `auditwheel show` returns non-empty rpath edits.
devon (infra): I can add a constraint file for builds: `constraints/pip-restrict.txt` with `tokenizers>=0.14.2`. Add to Dockerfiles with `pip install -c constraints/pip-restrict.txt -r requirements.txt`.
ci-bot: New pipeline job queued: #4156 - add pip constraint integration test 
priya (platform): Maria — can you open the security PR to block the versions and include language for Dedicated/Private? We need a notice for customers pinned to old locks.
maria (sec): Will do. Drafting advisory: recommend immediate lock-regen for any project that vendors tokenizers via poetry. Also recommend backporting patched wheels into our private wheel mirror for on-prem.
jon (ml): For model infra: I'll open an ML PR to pin transformers->tokenizers in `pyproject.toml` (we currently allow a range). Suggest `tokenizers = "^0.14.2"` in extras.
priya (platform): Also adding an automated check in `eng-releases` CI: after `poetry lock`, run `pip wheel --no-deps -w /tmp/wheels .` and run `auditwheel repair` and ensure no path traversal markers. If it fails, block the publish.
devon (infra): Quick mitigation for now: add Docker build step to drop to non-root user before pip install. That reduces blast radius. But long-term we must fix lockfiles.
sam (sre): We should also search our images for any occurrences where pip runs as root during runtime installs. I'll run `gcloud container images list --format=json` + grep script.
maria (sec): PRs: #1297 security/block-tokenizers-0.14.1, #1298 advisory/postmortem-draft. I'll include customer communication template for Dedicated/Private tenants and mitigation steps.
jon (ml): Note: regenerating poetry.lock bumped starlette -> 0.23.1 which conflicts with our pinned fastapi in tests (fastapi 0.88). That explains the other CI break.
priya (platform): Ugh — dependency graph churn. When you regenerate, please run `poetry lock --no-update` then `poetry update tokenizers` only, and run the tests. That minimizes drift.
devon (infra): If `poetry` still drifts, we can do a two-step approach: use `poetry lock --no-update` then edit `poetry.lock` to bump tokenizers hash and run `poetry install --no-dev` to validate. But that's hacky.
maria (sec): Decision: Emergency patch window — 24h to get constraint + private mirror backports + customer advisory. Assignments: Maria opens security PR + advisory, Devon adds pip constraint and non-root build step, Jon updates ML pyproject PR, Priya adds CI audit job, Sam runs image sweep.
jon (ml): I'll also add a smoke test for transformers CI that does `python -c "import tokenizers; print(tokenizers.__version__)"` after install and fails if version < 0.14.2.
priya (platform): Adding to backlog: automated KMS secret-check during build to ensure nothing writes to `/etc` or other sensitive paths. But not in the emergency window.
ci-bot: PR #1297 created by maria (sec) — https://git.redwood.internal/pulls/1297 :eyes:
maria (sec): Thanks all. I'll ping legal/comms once advisory is ready. :thumbsup:
